points.description: States that a linked list is a collection of elements (nodes) — i.e. a data structure made up of a collection of elements.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if it says it is a data structure/list of items but does not state it is a collection of elements/nodes.

points.description: States that these elements can be allocated dynamically (memory allocated at run time, as needed, not fixed in size in advance).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if it says only that the size can grow/shrink without naming dynamic allocation.

points.description: Correctly distinguishes it from an array: elements are not required to be in contiguous/fixed-size static memory, since they are allocated dynamically.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all three: a collection of elements, dynamic allocation stated with the correct term, and a correct contrast with a fixed-size/static array. Vague answers such as "a list of data" or "elements connected together" earn nothing on P2 or P3. Any wrong statement within a point (e.g. saying elements are stored contiguously or the size is fixed) means that point earns zero.
